text: git status shows the state of the working directory and staging area.
git add <file> stages changes in <file> for the next commit.
git commit -m "message" records staged changes with a message.
git push uploads local commits to a remote repository.
git pull fetches from a remote and merges into the current branch.
git branch <name> creates a new branch without switching to it.
git checkout -b <name> creates a new branch and switches to it immediately.
git switch <name> is the modern replacement for checkout when changing branches.
git log shows the commit history for the current branch.
git diff shows unstaged changes between the working directory and the last commit.
git stash temporarily shelves uncommitted changes so you can switch context.
git merge combines the history of another branch into the current branch.
git rebase replays commits from the current branch onto another base commit.
A pull request on GitHub proposes merging changes from one branch or fork into another, with room for review before it merges.
A GitHub Release packages a tagged version of the repository, usually with release notes and downloadable build artifacts.
GitHub Issues track bugs, tasks, and feature requests for a repository.
A fork on GitHub is a personal copy of someone else's repository, for making changes without affecting the original.
GitHub Actions runs automated workflows such as tests, builds, and deploys in response to repository events like a push.
